title: “One-in-1,000-Year” Rain Floods Florida's Space Coast as Cleanup Begins
dek: Melbourne recorded 11.04 inches of rain in 24 hours, breaking day, month and all-time records, as a state of emergency covered seven counties.

title: Four Corners Flooding Complicates Election-Day Voting for Some Residents
dek: Historically high rainfall and river flooding hit Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona and Utah for a second straight week, forcing evacuations and road closures.

title: New York Child Dies of Measles, the State's First Such Death in 30 Years
dek: State and county health departments announced the death Monday. New York had reported 178 measles cases as of October 24.

title: FDA Approves Generic Twice-Yearly HIV Prevention Shot for 120 Countries
dek: The generic version of lenacapavir is expected to cost $40 per person per year in low- and middle-income countries — but it cannot yet be sold as a generic in the U.S.

title: Kennedy Center Honors Move to Capital One Arena for 2026 Ceremony
dek: The 2026 honorees are Paul Anka, David Foster, Andy Garcia, David Mamet and Barbara Mandrell. The ceremony is set for December 7.

title: Russian Strike on Ukraine Aid Centre Kills at Least 26
dek: Ukrainian officials said aerial bombs hit a school used as a weekly aid distribution point in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region. Tuesday was declared a day of mourning.

title: Cyclone Murasu Makes Landfall on India's East Coast
dek: The severe cyclonic storm came ashore near Ongole in Andhra Pradesh early Tuesday, the second storm to hit the region in a week, with winds gusting to 120 km/h.

title: Belgium's Prime Minister Offers Resignation as Budget Talks Collapse
dek: Bart De Wever's five-party coalition failed to agree on about €10 billion in savings needed to meet EU deficit rules. King Philippe will consult party leaders from Tuesday.

title: One Killed as Two Helicopters Collide Near Mount Everest
dek: An Indian national was killed and a New Zealander injured as the helicopters prepared to land in Nepal's Everest region during peak trekking season.

title: Australia's High Court Hears Challenge to Under-16 Social Media Ban
dek: Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project argue the world-first ban violates an implied freedom of political communication. The government is defending the law.

title: Justice Department Sends 1,000 Election Monitors to All 50 States
dek: The department called it the largest monitoring effort in history. Voting-rights groups, including the NAACP, said the deployment could suppress turnout.

title: Supreme Court Rejects Bid to Set Aside 20,000 California Ballots
dek: No justices publicly dissented from the November 2 order, leaving California's existing ballot procedures in place on the eve of the midterms.

title: Justice Department Charges 63 People in Voting Cases Across 15 States
dek: The charges, announced one day before the midterms, include alleged illegal voting, fraudulent registration and false claims of U.S. citizenship. Charges are allegations, not convictions.

title: Judge Tosses Case Against Ex-FBI Officials Over Hunter Biden Probes
dek: A federal judge on Monday dismissed the criminal case accusing two former senior FBI officials of lying about their involvement in investigations into Hunter Biden.

title: 2026 Midterms on Track to Be the Most Expensive Ever at Nearly $12 Billion
dek: Spending is projected to rise 30 percent on 2022, according to OpenSecrets, with more than $9.5 billion already spent by mid-October.

title: Pfizer Raises 2026 Forecasts on Strong Eliquis and Cancer-Drug Demand
dek: The drugmaker lifted its sales forecast to $62 billion to $64 billion and named Cecile Guegan as chief financial officer effective November 1.

title: Bayer Raises 2026 Profit Outlook as Pharma Beats Expectations
dek: The German group lifted its adjusted core earnings outlook to €9.8 billion to €10.3 billion and said it expects a $7.25 billion Roundup settlement before Christmas.

title: Nasdaq-100 Enters Its Third Correction of 2026
dek: The index fell 10 percent from its most recent peak after a fresh sell-off in technology stocks, its worst monthly performance since March 2025.

title: Asian Stocks Fall as U.S. Chip Sell-Off Spreads
dek: South Korea's Kospi fell more than 3.34 percent and Taiwan's TAIEX lost 1.21 percent, while Japanese markets were shut for Culture Day.

title: Marvell Agrees to Buy Lumentum in $115 Billion All-Stock Deal
dek: Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares per share, with Marvell holders owning about 67 percent of the combined company. The deal is expected to close in the first half of calendar 2028.

title: Baidu Launches Apollo World AI Simulator for Robotaxis
dek: The system can generate up to 100,000 km of simulated driving daily — equivalent to about three years of real-world testing by a safety-driver-equipped vehicle.

title: Apple Removes 19 Apps After WIRED Uncovers 400-App Deepfake Network
dek: The apps appeared to offer harmless services like pet portraits and fitness coaching, but could secretly load tools for generating sexually abusive deepfakes.

title: Anthropic Reports $17 Billion in Third-Quarter Revenue Ahead of IPO
dek: Revenue rose 47 percent from the second quarter, but the company reported a $23.29 billion net loss and $895.4 billion in purchase commitments and leases.

title: Apple Intelligence Comes to China on Alibaba's Qwen, Testing November 4
dek: Alibaba said user requests and responses will not be used to train models, with participation opt-in. The redesigned Siri announced at WWDC is not in this phase.

title: CrowdStrike Unveils AI Kill Switch and Planned Fiddler Acquisition
dek: Announced at Fal.Con Europe in Barcelona, the Falcon Guardian feature is designed to stop unauthorized agent activity at runtime and block it from running again.

title: Ariana Grande Played Unreleased Music on the Set of 'Focker-in-Law'
dek: Co-star Skyler Gisondo told The Hollywood Reporter that after she played new material, he told her, “Nobody should be able to do this.”

title: Michael Jackson Biopic 'MICHAEL' Earns Three Hollywood Music in Media Awards Nominations
dek: Jaafar Jackson was nominated for his onscreen performance of “Bad,” director Antoine Fuqua for Music-Themed Film, and John Warhurst for music supervision.

title: 'Ramayana' Breaks Pre-Diwali Advance-Booking Record With Rs. 25 Crore-Plus
dek: PVR INOX executive Kamal Gianchandani said the film is on course for the biggest pre-Diwali advance bookings in the chain's 30-plus-year history.

title: 'Whalefall' Loses 1,000 Theaters in Its Third Week
dek: The survival thriller fell from 3,065 theaters at its October 16 opening to 2,000, with a worldwide total of about $36.87 million against a reported $60 million production cost.

title: Original 'John Wick' Finally Opens in China, Debuting at No. 3
dek: The 2014 action film was rejected by Chinese regulators in 2015 as too violent. It opened October 30 with $2.3 million over three days.

title: Bears Rout Seahawks 34-17 on Monday Night Football
dek: D'Andre Swift rushed for three second-half touchdowns as Chicago won its third in a row since Caleb Williams returned from a hamstring injury.

title: Pelicans Hand Grizzlies First Loss in Overtime Thriller, 135-134
dek: Jeremiah Fears sank two clutch free throws with 7.3 seconds left in overtime as New Orleans ended Memphis' franchise-record-matching six-game winning streak.

title: Doncic Drops 42 as Lakers Rout Heat 138-117
dek: It was Doncic's fourth 40-point game this season and came one night after a 45-point game against Toronto, lifting the Lakers to 6-2.

title: NBA Goes Dark on Election Day to Promote the Midterm Vote
dek: The league scheduled no games on Tuesday, November 3, for the fourth time in five years, to encourage fans and the broader NBA community to vote.

title: Curry's 34 Lifts Warriors Past Suns 116-113
dek: Stephen Curry added 7 assists, 6 rebounds and 5 three-pointers, and Brandin Podziemski added 20 points as Golden State improved to 5-3.

title: Nine Dead After Bahamas-Bound Jet Plunges Into Florida Neighborhood
dek: A Learjet 60 carrying nine people crashed in Palm Beach County on Sunday afternoon, killing everyone on board and narrowly missing homes.

title: Halloween Weekend Turns Deadly Across America as Shootings Hit Dallas, Birmingham, and College Towns
dek: At least 15 people were killed and dozens more injured in shootings across the United States over Halloween weekend, with the deadliest cluster in Dallas.

title: Indicted ICE Officer to Surrender After Houston SUV Strike Leaves Man Seriously Injured
dek: A Harris County grand jury indicted ICE officer Mario Alberto Morales on aggravated assault after an October 10 incident in which his SUV struck a man fleeing on foot.

title: 'Ghost Students' Stole Millions in Federal Aid, Justice Department Charges in Nationwide Crackdown
dek: The Justice Department unveiled the first charges in 'Operation Ghostbusters,' a nationwide probe into fake college students created with stolen identities to siphon federal student aid.

title: Schools Must Now Justify Every Federal Dollar in 255 Characters, or Wait to Get Paid
dek: Starting November 1, every recipient of U.S. Department of Education grant money must attach a written justification of no more than 255 characters to each payment request.

title: Democrat Stuns Her Own Party, Endorses Republican in Michigan Senate Race Two Days Before Election
dek: Rep. Haley Stevens, who lost Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, endorsed Republican Mike Rogers on Sunday in one of the races that could decide control of the Senate.

title: Senator Chris Murphy Hospitalized After Stroke at Son's Hockey Game, Office Expects Full Recovery
dek: The Connecticut Democrat, 53, was transferred to Johns Hopkins for monitoring and is awake and alert, his office said Sunday.

title: Judge Throws Out DOJ's Alaska Election Lawsuit, Then the Department Appeals Within the Hour
dek: A federal judge ruled two days before Election Day that the government lacked a workable legal remedy to block Alaska from certifying its Senate election.

title: Trump to Deliver Final Midterm Pitch at Reflecting Pool, and Warns of Vetoes If Democrats Win Congress
dek: The president caps a final blitz Monday afternoon in Washington, framing Tuesday's vote as a choice over vetoes, subpoenas, and the last two years of his agenda.

title: Trump Says U.S. and Canada Have the 'Concept' of a New Trade Deal After Talks With Carney
dek: Both leaders described constructive talks but no signed agreement, with teams set to work in the coming weeks on terms including tariffs.

title: Bulgaria Elects First Woman President as Yotova Wins Runoff With 57.6%
dek: Acting president Iliana Yotova won Sunday's runoff in a landslide, becoming the first woman ever elected to Bulgaria's highest office.

title: 320,000 Take to France's Streets for Third Weekend of Youth-Led Protests
dek: Turnout fell from the two previous Saturdays, but marches across France still ended in tear gas, scattered fires, and more than 560 arrests.

title: UN Ends 35-Year Western Sahara Peacekeeping Mission After Security Council Deadlock
dek: MINURSO ceased operations Sunday after the Security Council failed to agree on its future, ending a mission that monitored a ceasefire since 1991.

title: Commonwealth Leaders Descend on Antigua as King Charles Faces Slavery Reckoning
dek: More than 50 leaders are meeting in Antigua for the Commonwealth summit, where the King is set to address Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade.

title: Spain Names 66 of 69 Dead in Urda Train Crash, Including Four Americans
dek: Forensic teams have identified nearly all victims of the October 28 high-speed collision, with three people still unidentified and three missing-person cases open.

title: South Korea Nears $1 Trillion in Annual Exports as Chip Sales Nearly Triple
dek: October exports jumped 93.7% to $115.28 billion, with semiconductors alone accounting for nearly half of everything the country shipped abroad.

title: FBI Blames North Korea for $6.3 Billion Binance Heist, the Biggest Crypto Theft Ever
dek: The FBI attributed the record theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor unit as Binance resumed withdrawals after covering about 95% of the stolen assets.

title: OPEC+ Keeps December Oil Targets on Hold for a Third Straight Month
dek: Seven core producers agreed to leave December targets unchanged as Brent crude enters November above $110 a barrel.

title: Apple's New Chief Faces First Earnings Test as Memory Costs Bite
dek: John Ternus hosts his first earnings call as Apple's CEO on Monday, with investors watching the holiday-quarter forecast for signs new products can offset surging memory costs.

title: Global Manufacturing Holds Firm in October as Energy Costs Bite
dek: Factory surveys show activity still growing, but rising energy costs and supply disruptions are squeezing margins on both sides of the Atlantic.

title: Motorola's Signature 27 Leaks in Full Ahead of November 5 Launch: 12,000-Nit Display, 200MP Camera
dek: A hands-on video has revealed Motorola's next premium flagship in detail days before its global launch, including a Tandem OLED screen and seven years of OS updates.

title: Google Gets Its First AI Answer Back From a Chip in Orbit
dek: A prototype satellite running a Gemma model on a data-center-class TPU has returned its first AI-generated response from space, Google's Project Suncatcher team says.

title: Microsoft 365 Family Users Are Losing Their Individual 1TB, and Sharing Just 2TB Instead
dek: Microsoft has reshaped one of its most popular subscriptions, cutting total cloud storage for a full Family plan by two-thirds while keeping the price the same.

title: Claude Will No Longer Rebuild Your Favorite Video Game for You
dek: Anthropic has drawn a clearer line around what its AI assistant can do with video games, blocking it from recreating existing titles even when users try to disguise the copy.

title: Judge Refuses to Throw Out NAACP Pollution Lawsuit Over xAI's Memphis-Area Data Center
dek: A federal judge ruled the Clean Air Act case against xAI can proceed, rejecting the company's bid to have it dismissed.

title: A Documentary Just Beat a Superhero Movie at the Halloween Box Office, by $200,000
dek: Halloween weekend produced one of the closest box-office finishes of the year, with A24's Elizabeth Holmes documentary edging out DC's 'Clayface.'

title: Jesse Eisenberg's 'The Debut' to Open the Marrakech Film Festival
dek: The comedy starring Julianne Moore as a shy housewife turned zealous Method actor will open the festival's 23rd edition on November 20.

title: Japan's Anime Market Hits a Record $28.2 Billion, and Most of the Money Now Comes From Abroad
dek: Worldwide spending on Japanese anime reached a record 4.45 trillion yen in 2025, with overseas fans now accounting for 57.1% of the total.

title: Taylor Swift Reveals the 20-Year Inside Joke She Still Shares With Her Best Friend
dek: At a 'Toy Story 5' screening in New York, Swift told the audience she and Abigail Anderson Berard have bonded over 'Napoleon Dynamite' voices since high school, and never stopped.

title: JYP Says It Never Got Nexroc's Takeover Bid: The Email Was Blocked as Spam
dek: As Nexroc's November 2 proposal deadline passed with no confirmed offer, JYP said the investor's email never reached the company and regulators are watching the saga.

title: At 20, Kimi Antonelli Becomes Formula 1's Youngest-Ever World Champion
dek: The Mercedes driver's third place in a dramatic, red-flagged Mexico City Grand Prix sealed the title with an unassailable 119-point lead.

title: Canelo Is Champion Again After Outpointing Mbilli in Riyadh
dek: The Mexican star reclaimed the WBC super middleweight title on scorecards of 117-110, 116-111, and 115-112 in his first fight in 13 months.

title: Bayern's Klassiker Draw Comes at a Heavy Price: Saibari and Gnabry Out Indefinitely
dek: Bayern confirmed Sunday that Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry are out indefinitely after both were forced off in the first half of Saturday's 2-2 draw with Dortmund.

title: Minnesota Stuns LAFC 3-1 to Keep Its Playoff Dream Alive
dek: Joaquín Pereyra scored twice as Minnesota beat LAFC at BMO Stadium, moving within two points of the final playoff spots with one match left.

title: Messi's Late Winner Lifts Inter Miami Past New England and Into Second in the East
dek: Messi assisted the equalizer and scored his league-leading 26th goal in the 83rd minute as Miami completed a 2-1 comeback at Gillette Stadium.

title: JUDGE TO DOJ: STOP THREATENING ELECTION OFFICIALS DAYS BEFORE THE MIDTERMS
dek: A federal judge has ordered the Justice Department and Homeland Security to stop threatening state and local election officials with prosecution over ballots the administration claims may come from noncitizens — a temporary order running through November 16.

title: CASE CLOSED: JUDGE PERMANENTLY DISMISSES TRUMP'S $10 BILLION SUIT AGAINST THE WALL STREET JOURNAL
dek: President Donald Trump's second attempt to sue the Wall Street Journal over its reporting on his ties to Jeffrey Epstein was dismissed with prejudice on Saturday, meaning it cannot be brought again.

title: NEWSOM WARNS CALIFORNIA JUDGES: FEDS MAY TRY TO SEIZE BALLOTS BEFORE CERTIFICATION
dek: California Governor Gavin Newsom warned the state's top federal judges on Saturday that the Justice Department may seek warrants to seize ballots and ballot materials before results are certified, Reuters reported.

title: TEXAS EARLY VOTE EXPLODES: 6.3 MILLION ALREADY CAST, UP 50% FROM 2022
dek: Texas voters are turning out early in huge numbers, with more than 6.3 million ballots cast before Election Day — a 50% jump from the same point four years ago — as competitive Senate, House and governor's races drive a national early-vote surge.

title: POPE LEO PLAYS REFEREE AS VILLANOVA AND NOTRE DAME DESCEND ON THE VATICAN
dek: Pope Leo, the first American pope, received his alma mater Villanova and its rival Notre Dame at the Vatican on Saturday — greeting both schools' men's and women's basketball teams before roughly 7,000 players, guests and supporters.

title: ISRAELI STRIKES KILL EIGHT IN GAZA AS YEAR-OLD CEASEFIRE FRAYS FURTHER
dek: Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians in Gaza on Sunday, including five police officers in Khan Younis and three people in Gaza City, according to medics and the Hamas-run interior ministry.

title: HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS LEFT WITHOUT POWER AS RUSSIA POUNDS UKRAINE'S GRID
dek: Russian strikes hit power infrastructure in four Ukrainian regions overnight, cutting electricity to hundreds of thousands of households, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Sunday — even as a local ceasefire held its final day around Oleshky.

title: SUPERTANKER HITS NAVAL MINE AND CATCHES FIRE IN THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ
dek: A supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of oil struck a naval mine and caught fire while using an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guard said Friday — the fourth tanker explosion there that day.

title: NETANYAHU'S PARTY CLAIMS ISRAEL'S ELECTION WAS STOLEN. NOW WHAT?
dek: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party alleged Thursday that Israel's election earlier in the week was stolen by Arab-majority parties, helped by foreign funding that amounted to vote-buying — as final results showed Netanyahu's bloc has lost its majority in the Knesset.

title: TRUMP SAYS DEFEATED BRAZILIAN CANDIDATE FLAVIO BOLSONARO CAN STAY IN THE U.S. INDEFINITELY
dek: President Donald Trump said on Saturday evening that defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro can stay in the United States indefinitely, Reuters reported.

title: TWO DAYS OUT: POLLS PUT DEMOCRATS AHEAD — AND TRUMP AT A RECORD LOW
dek: With two days to go before the midterms, Democrats lead Republicans on the generic ballot by double digits in some surveys, while President Donald Trump's approval has fallen to 31–32% — the lowest of his presidency in the Reuters/Ipsos and CNN polls.

title: THE VOTERS WHO HELPED PUT TRUMP BACK IN THE WHITE HOUSE ARE WALKING AWAY
dek: Just 24% of Latino registered voters approve of President Donald Trump's job performance, down from 38% at the start of his second term, according to a Pew Research Center survey — and Democrats lead Republicans 51% to 24% among Latino voters in House races.

title: KANSAS SHOCKER: DEMOCRAT LEADS A REPUBLICAN SENATOR IN POLL AFTER POLL
dek: A Washington Post-Schar School poll shows Democrat Adam Hamilton leading Republican Senator Roger Marshall 52% to 43% in Kansas, with an Emerson College survey showing a tighter 50% to 47% — a race that would have been unthinkable a cycle ago.

title: THE SUPREME COURT ISN'T ON THE BALLOT — BUT IT'S ON VOTERS' MINDS
dek: No justices are up for election Tuesday, but the results of the November 3 contests could shape disputes about the high court's membership, its size and its ethics, USA Today reported.

title: THE MOST EXPENSIVE MIDTERMS EVER: $11.6 BILLION AND COUNTING
dek: The 2026 midterm campaign is projected to cost $11.6 billion, surpassing even the $11.2 billion spent in the 2024 presidential cycle, according to AdImpact, which tracks broadcast advertising.

title: GULF MARKETS SLIDE ON IRAN WAR FEARS — BUT QATAR SURGES 4.6%
dek: Gulf stock markets fell on Sunday as investors braced for the risk of renewed conflict between the United States and Iran after the midterms — except in Qatar, where the benchmark jumped 4.6% in its sharpest intraday gain in more than eight years.

title: OCTOBER SPLIT THE MARKET IN TWO: NASDAQ DOWN 5.3%, DOW UP 1.7%
dek: October just split the world's stock markets in two: tech-heavy indexes bled red while blue chips held green, with the Nasdaq down 5.3% on the month and the Dow up 1.7%.

title: ALPHABET'S $127.6 BILLION QUARTER STILL WASN'T ENOUGH — SHARES FELL 13%
dek: Alphabet's revenue rose 25% year over year to $127.6 billion in the third quarter, but net income fell 25% to $26.2 billion — far below the $37.3 billion expected — and shares fell 13% in after-hours trading.

title: AMAZON MADE $201.9 BILLION — AND STILL BURNED $33.5 BILLION IN CASH
dek: Amazon's total revenue came in at $201.9 billion in the third quarter, while net income fell to $20.7 billion and free cash flow turned negative at a loss of $33.5 billion, as AI capital spending surged to $75.8 billion in the quarter.

title: SHOULD YOU BUY STOCKS BEFORE THE MIDTERMS? HISTORY SAYS YES — EVERY TIME
dek: Since 1950, investors buying at the end of October in a midterm year have been treated to positive 12-month S&P 500 gains 100% of the time, with an average return of 16.6%, according to the Motley Fool.

title: CHAINALYSIS DISCLOSES BREACH USING 'OFFENSIVE AGENTIC TECHNIQUES'
dek: Chainalysis says an attacker gained access to internal systems using what it describes as offensive agentic techniques, accessing customer names, email addresses, user IDs and organisational role labels — but no investigation content, credentials or session tokens.

title: VOLTA MALWARE USES AI TO RANK ITS VICTIMS — AND PICK THE RICHEST TARGETS
dek: Cisco Talos reported on October 31 that the VOLTA infostealer can send a structured bundle of stolen information to an AI model to assess a victim's assets and security posture, using a fallback chain of Claude Opus 4.6, Kimi K2 and Gemini 2.5 Flash.

title: ALIBABA'S QWEN ENTERS APPLE INTELLIGENCE IN CHINA — BETA STARTS NOVEMBER 4
dek: Alibaba announced that its Qwen model will be integrated into Apple Intelligence for China, with testing starting in the iOS developer beta on November 4 and a public release planned for December.

title: MISTRAL OPENS THE WEIGHTS OF LARGE 4, ITS 1-TRILLION-PARAMETER FLAGSHIP
dek: Mistral calls Large 4 'our flagship 1-trillion-parameter, natively multimodal model,' with weights on Hugging Face and self-hosting via vLLM or SGLang — but businesses offering it as a service need a separate commercial licence.

title: OPENAI'S GPT-6.1 TERRA COSTS HALF AS MUCH — AND THE PRICE WAR IS ON
dek: OpenAI says GPT-6.1 Terra's standard API prices are 50% lower than those of GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, at $1 per million input tokens, $0.05 per million cached input tokens, and $5 per million output tokens.

title: JAILER 2 IS ₹9 CRORE AWAY FROM ₹800 CRORE WORLDWIDE
dek: Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 is closing in on the ₹800 crore worldwide milestone after 17 days in theatres, collecting an estimated ₹9.35 crore net in India on Saturday, October 31.

title: MARVEL CONFIRMS IT: AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY WILL BE PATRICK STEWART'S FINAL ROLE
dek: Marvel Studios has confirmed that Avengers: Doomsday, which opens on December 18, will be Sir Patrick Stewart's final onscreen performance, ending a 26-year run as Professor Xavier.

title: SHAH RUKH KHAN PERSONALLY CALLED ADITYA CHOPRA BEFORE MOVING KING'S OVERSEAS DEAL
dek: Shah Rukh Khan personally spoke to Yash Raj Films chief Aditya Chopra before shifting King's overseas distribution to Phars Films, Bollywood Hungama has learned — and Chopra gave his blessings.

title: PRIYANKA CHOPRA CHANNELS 'KING KYLIE' FOR HALLOWEEN WITH NICK JONAS AND MALTI MARIE
dek: Priyanka Chopra Jonas channelled 'King Kylie' for Halloween alongside Nick Jonas and their daughter Malti Marie, Bollywood Hungama reported on November 1.

title: MYSAA DROPS PROMO FOR FIRST SONG 'O MYSAA RE' — FULL TRACK OUT NOVEMBER 2
dek: The makers of Mysaa, starring Rashmika Mandanna, have unveiled a promo for the film's first single, 'O Mysaa Re', with the track scheduled for release on November 2.

title: USC STUNS NO. 2 OHIO STATE 30-18 AT THE COLISEUM
dek: USC stunned No. 2 Ohio State 30-18 at the Coliseum on Saturday, the headline result of a Week 9 Saturday that saw seven ranked teams lose and the College Football Playoff picture come sharply into focus.

title: GEORGIA 27, FLORIDA 8: BULLDOGS' DEFENSE SUPPLIES THE ANSWER IN ATLANTA
dek: Georgia's offensive performance was far from convincing — just 101 passing yards — but the Bulldogs' defense controlled the line of scrimmage, limited Florida's Jadan Baugh to 38 yards on 17 carries, and recorded 11 tackles for loss in a 27-8 rout.

title: DURANT, SMART POWER ROCKETS PAST THUNDER 119-98
dek: Kevin Durant recorded 14 points, four assists and three blocks as the Houston Rockets beat the Oklahoma City Thunder 119-98 on Saturday, with Marcus Smart adding 24 points.

title: COURT REINSTATES 'SUNDAY TICKET' VERDICT AGAINST THE NFL — BUT ORDERS NEW TRIAL ON DAMAGES
dek: A U.S. federal appeals court on Friday reinstated a jury's verdict against the NFL in an antitrust lawsuit claiming it overcharged subscribers to its Sunday Ticket game telecasts for more than a decade — but said the league can have a new trial on damages.

title: SHNAIDER DOWNS FERNANDEZ TO CLAIM PAN PACIFIC OPEN TITLE IN TOKYO
dek: Russia's Diana Shnaider overcame a second-set collapse to beat Canada's Leylah Fernandez 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 on Sunday and claim the Pan Pacific Open title in Tokyo.

title: Burger King Drive-Thru Worker in Blackface Tells Customers She 'Just Wanted to Be Black'
dek: A 28-second clip filmed at a Burger King drive-thru window has gone viral after a worker with her face painted black told the customers filming her she 'just wanted to be Black' — an exchange that has now been viewed millions of times on X.

title: 49 MILLION VOTES ALREADY CAST: MIDTERMS HEAD INTO FINAL WEEKEND WITH RECORD EARLY TURNOUT
dek: More Americans have voted early in this midterm than in 2022, with all 435 House seats and 35 Senate races on the ballot Tuesday — and control of Congress, and the shape of Donald Trump's final two years, on the line.

title: FOUR CHARGED IN $41 MILLION MINNESOTA HEALTH CARE FRAUD SWEEP
dek: Federal officials announced charges against four people in Minnesota on Friday, alleging a scheme to defraud health programs of more than $41 million — and unveiled a new order to trace money diverted overseas.

title: JUDGE BLOCKS MEDICAID RULE THAT FORCED SICK PATIENTS TO PROVE THEY CAN'T WORK
dek: A federal judge has blocked a Trump administration rule that required Medicaid recipients in medical-frailty categories to prove their condition keeps them from meeting new work requirements.

title: MORE THAN 150 AFGHANS FACE DEPORTATION IN ONE OF THE LARGEST SINGLE EXPULSIONS
dek: The Trump administration plans to deport more than 150 Afghan immigrants, with dozens already detained in Louisiana and a first flight expected as soon as Monday, Reuters reported Friday.

title: MORE THAN 100 CATS RESCUED FROM HORROR HOUSE — WOMAN FACES 29 FELONY COUNTS
dek: A 66-year-old Florida woman was arrested Thursday on dozens of animal cruelty counts after more than 100 cats and kittens were removed from a Port St. Lucie home, police said.

title: STRONG GROWTH, STUBBORN INFLATION: THE ECONOMY HANDS VOTERS A MIXED BAG DAYS BEFORE THE MIDTERMS
dek: The economy grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, but consumer prices rose 3.6% from a year earlier — a split picture landing less than a week before Election Day.

title: BACK ON: TRUMP REVIVES KANSAS AND IOWA RALLIES AFTER ABRUPT CANCELLATION
dek: President Donald Trump will hold rallies for Senate midterm candidates in Kansas and Iowa on Sunday after previously canceling the visits days before the election, USA Today reported.

title: COURT TO CALIFORNIA BALLOT CHALLENGE: NO — APPEALS PANEL REJECTS TRUMP BID AGAIN
dek: A federal appeals court on Friday rejected the Trump administration's latest attempt to stop California from counting mail ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters the government alleges are likely noncitizens.

title: THE $54-A-MONTH SQUEEZE: ENERGY BILLS BITE SWING-STATE VOTERS BEFORE TUESDAY
dek: Households in the states most likely to decide control of Congress are paying $50 to $60 more a month for power and gasoline than a year ago, Reuters reported Saturday.

title: HEGSETH FIRES PENTAGON'S TOP WAR PLANNER OVER ALLEGED LEAKS
dek: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, the Pentagon's top military planner, on Thursday over accusations he disclosed classified information to journalists.

title: PUTIN COURTS AFRICA — BUT LEADERS PLAY THEIR OWN GAME IN MOSCOW
dek: Russia hosted its third Russia-Africa Summit this week, with Vladimir Putin pitching Moscow as a better partner than the West — while African leaders pursued deals on their own terms.

title: MANURE ON THE STREETS OF TURIN: ITALY ERUPTS IN 50-CITY PROTEST WAVE
dek: Tens of thousands took to the streets across more than 50 Italian cities on Friday to protest soaring living costs and crumbling public services, with farmers dumping manure in Turin.

title: POLAND ON EDGE: PRESIDENT ABORTS SENEGAL TRIP AS COURT CRISIS SPARKS OVERNIGHT PROTESTS
dek: Hundreds of protesters rallied overnight around Poland's top court to denounce the suspension of the tribunal's president, and President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane home mid-flight.

title: 70,000 POLICE ON THE STREETS AS FRANCE BRACES FOR HALLOWEEN UNREST
dek: France deployed a 70,000-strong police presence on Saturday for the latest nationwide protests over living costs and public services — two weeks after riots and looting caught security forces off guard.

title: ZELENSKY WELCOMES $2.1 BILLION PATRIOT DEAL — BUT WARNS THE MISSILES COULD TAKE YEARS
dek: Ukraine's president welcomed U.S. approval of a potential sale of 500 Patriot interceptor missiles on Friday, while warning it may take 'a few years' for them to arrive.

title: WAGE GROWTH COOLS: U.S. LABOR COSTS RISE MORE SLOWLY IN THIRD QUARTER
dek: U.S. labor costs increased moderately in the third quarter amid a slowdown in wage growth, suggesting the labor market was unlikely to be an inflation risk, Reuters reported Friday.

title: AFTER THE $6.3 BILLION BINANCE HEIST, CRYPTO EXCHANGES RACE TO LOCK THE DOORS
dek: Crypto exchanges moved quickly to bolster defenses after a record $6.3 billion hack of Binance exposed their vulnerability just as they become more embedded in mainstream finance.

title: VIRGIN MEDIA O2 TO CUT THOUSANDS OF JOBS IN SWEEPING SHAKEUP
dek: British telecoms operator Virgin Media O2 will cut thousands of jobs, Sky News reported Saturday, with up to 4,000 of its 16,000 employees potentially affected.

title: NETFLIX DOWN A THIRD THIS YEAR — AND THE CHARTS SAY MORE PAIN COULD COME
dek: Shares in Netflix have lost about a third of their value this year, hurt most recently by disappointing guidance, and technical signals point to further downside, Reuters reported.

title: ANTHROPIC'S IPO FILING REVEALS 1,368% REVENUE SURGE — AND A HALF-TRILLION SPENDING BILL
dek: Anthropic filed for an IPO this week, and its prospectus gave a clearer view of the AI company's growth — eye-popping revenue growth paired with spending commitments of more than half a trillion dollars.

title: APPLE CAVES AT LAST: FIRST TOUCHSCREEN MACBOOK PRO ARRIVES WITH PROLED DISPLAY
dek: Apple announced its first laptop with a touchscreen on October 28, ending years of resistance to touch on the Mac — with a tandem OLED panel, M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and prices starting at $2,899.

title: FCC CLEARS AMAZON'S $11.5 BILLION GLOBALSTAR DEAL IN SATELLITE RACE WITH STARLINK
dek: The FCC approved Amazon Leo's $11.5 billion acquisition of Globalstar on October 27, clearing Amazon's satellite arm to build a communications network to compete with SpaceX's Starlink.

title: MALICIOUS 'CLAUDE CODE' COPY SLIPPED INTO CURSOR'S MARKETPLACE FOR 11 HOURS
dek: A malicious copy of extension versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 was available in Cursor's marketplace for about 11 hours on October 29, Cursor said — while Microsoft separately detailed intrusions posing as IT support.

title: GOOGLE AI PLUS LOSES ITS PRO MODELS — AND VERIZON SIGNS A $2 BILLION AWS DEAL
dek: Google AI Plus, the cheapest of Google's AI plans, stops offering Pro models in the Gemini app and in AI Mode in Search from November 13 — while Verizon unveiled a $2 billion-plus AI infrastructure deal with Amazon Web Services.

title: ONE SWITCH TO OPT OUT: AI GIANTS BACK A SHARED 'DO NOT TRAIN' SIGNAL FOR PUBLISHERS
dek: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic said on October 30 they plan to recognize one shared robots.txt signal letting websites opt out of having their content used to train generative AI models.

title: HARRYWEEN IS BACK: STYLES OPENS AS ELVIS, THEN BECOMES HIS 16-YEAR-OLD SELF
dek: Harry Styles brought back Harryween at Madison Square Garden on Friday, opening as Elvis Presley before changing into the outfit from his 2010 X Factor audition.

title: SNL'S HALLOWEEN NIGHT: INDE NAVARRETTE HOSTS, GRACIE ABRAMS PERFORMS
dek: Saturday Night Live returns from its two-week hiatus with a Halloween night episode on Saturday, hosted by Inde Navarrette with Gracie Abrams as musical guest.

title: GHOSTBUSTERS TANGO AND A FIRST-EVER TRIPLE DANCE-OFF: STRICTLY'S HALLOWEEN SPECIAL
dek: Strictly Come Dancing's Halloween Special airs Saturday night with 11 couples dancing everything from a Ghostbusters tango to a Little Mix quickstep — and Sunday brings the first triple dance-off in the show's history.

title: HALLOWEEN WEEKEND WATCH LIST: GILDED AGE, DEXTER AND A MATTHEW PERRY DOC
dek: New streaming releases for the weekend of October 30 to November 1 include the Season 4 premiere of HBO's The Gilded Age, Season 2 of Dexter: Resurrection, and a three-part Matthew Perry documentary.

title: A QUIET HALLOWEEN BOX OFFICE CROWNS AN UNLIKELY QUEEN: THE ELIZABETH HOLMES DOC
dek: With Halloween falling on a Saturday and every major distributor sitting the frame out, A24's Elizabeth Holmes documentary 'You Can See Everything' is forecast to top the box office in its third weekend.

title: PANTHERS FIRE DEFENSIVE COORDINATOR EVERO HOURS AFTER PRIMETIME COLLAPSE
dek: The Carolina Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero on Friday, less than half a day after his unit collapsed again in primetime in a 27-19 defeat at Lambeau Field.

title: FINED AGAIN: CALEB WILLIAMS HIT WITH $23,882 OVER NON-PARTNER CLEATS — AND HE'S NOT STOPPING
dek: The NFL fined Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams for the second time over his choice of footwear, ESPN reported — $23,882 for sporting Caddix cleats in the Week 7 win against New England.

title: NBA CUP NIGHT ONE: LEBRON LIFTS SIXERS PAST KNICKS, CURRY ERASES 25-POINT DEFICIT
dek: On the first night of NBA Cup play on Friday, LeBron James delivered late as Philadelphia edged New York 98-93, while Stephen Curry poured in 31 as Golden State rallied past the Lakers 112-95.

title: CHANDLER SMITH TAKES MARTINSVILLE AS HONEYCUTT CARRIES 20-POINT LEAD TO THE FINALE
dek: Chandler Smith and the No. 38 Front Row Motorsports team won the Black's Tire 200 at Martinsville Speedway, their third victory of the 2026 NASCAR Truck Series season.

title: SIX DAYS AFTER STUNNING NO. 2 BYU, UCF GETS CRUSHED 41-9 BY BAYLOR
dek: Six days after stunning No. 2 BYU in double overtime, UCF returned home and was crushed 41-9 by unranked Baylor, snapping the Knights' four-game home winning streak.

title: TRAPPED FOR YEARS, THEY FINALLY GOT OUT: Hundreds Evacuate Besieged Oleshky Under Fragile Ceasefire
dek: After months cut off from food, medicine and power, residents of the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky began leaving Friday under a temporary truce — but the road out is long, and the ceasefire is set to expire Sunday.

title: BREWERS DO IT AT LAST: First World Series Title in 57 Years
dek: Milwaukee beat Tampa Bay 4-1 in Game 5 to cap a dominant 11-2 playoff run and finally bring a championship home to Wisconsin.

title: WALL STREET'S OCTOBER ENDS IN A BLOODBATH AS AI SPENDING PANIC TORCHES TECH
dek: The Nasdaq just suffered its worst day since June and its worst month since March 2025, as investors finally balked at the eye-watering price tag of the AI boom.

title: TRUMP HITS ROCK BOTTOM DAYS BEFORE THE MIDTERMS
dek: A new Emerson College poll puts President Donald Trump's approval at just 37% — his lowest ever in that poll — with Democrats opening a double-digit lead on the generic ballot four days before Election Day.

title: ESCAPED KILLER STILL ON THE RUN — AND PRISON WAITED HOURS TO SOUND THE ALARM
dek: A convicted murderer cut his way out of a Tennessee prison, stole a truck, and was already across state lines before outside police were told — and investigators are now probing a possible link to a Wisconsin bank robbery.

title: FAITHFULS WIN THE CASTLE: Romesh and Sebastian Take Celebrity Traitors
dek: After weeks of deception at Ardross Castle, two Faithfuls outlasted the Traitors and split £83,000 for charity in a dramatic final.

title: INTEL'S WARNING SPOOKS THE ENTIRE CHIP WORLD
dek: Intel's bleak forecast wiped tens of billions off its own value and dragged chip stocks down around the globe, as weak PC demand and rising memory costs squeeze the industry.

title: NO SMILES FOR THE CAMERA: G20 Ministers Skip Group Photo Over Russia
dek: G20 foreign ministers skipped their traditional family photo in Atlanta on Friday after European ministers refused to pose alongside Russia's Sergei Lavrov.

title: RECORD KING TIDES SWAMP BOTH COASTS: Streets Turned Into Canals
dek: From Los Angeles Harbor to Miami, the October king tides smashed century-old records, flooded beach neighborhoods, shut roads, and pushed one city to declare a local emergency.

title: JUSTICE FOR GLITTER: Mariah Carey Opens the Vault for 25th Anniversary
dek: Mariah Carey marked 25 years of Glitter with a 27-track deluxe edition packed with vault recordings, remixes, and live tracks.

title: FORECASTER SHIFTS 14 RACES TOWARD DEMS: And a Blue Wave Is Now on the Table
dek: The Cook Political Report moved 14 House and Senate races in Democrats' favor on October 30, raising the prospect of the party's biggest House majority in more than a decade.

title: AMAZON'S $220 BILLION AI BET SPOOKS WALL STREET AS CASH BLEEDS OUT
dek: Amazon told investors its AI spending spree is only getting bigger — projecting about $220 billion in capital spending next year — and the market punished the stock for it.

title: HEGSETH FIRES PENTAGON'S TOP WAR PLANNER AS IRAN STRIKES LOOM
dek: The Pentagon's chief planning officer was abruptly ousted over alleged classified leaks — just as U.S. forces in the Middle East stand ready to launch major new operations against Iran.

title: NETFLIX SAYS YES AGAIN: The Diplomat Renewed for Season 5
dek: Just two weeks after Season 4 dropped, Netflix confirmed Keri Russell's political thriller will return for a fifth season.

title: INDIA'S NAVIGATION SATELLITE BLASTS OFF: And Restores Its GPS Rival to Full Strength
dek: India's GSLV-F18 rocket lifted off late on October 30 carrying the NVS-03 navigation satellite, which ISRO confirmed reached its intended orbit.

title: A DECADE WITHOUT A VOTE: Haiti Finally Sets Election Dates for 2027
dek: Haiti will hold its first elections in more than a decade in July and October 2027, authorities announced — but gangs control large parts of the country, and whether voting can actually happen remains an open question.

title: AMBULANCE TO HERO: Watson Leaves in an Ambulance, Comes Back to Seal Packers Win
dek: Christian Watson was taken to a hospital for a chest injury in the first half — then returned to Lambeau Field and helped Green Bay beat Carolina 27-19 on Thursday Night Football.

title: JUDGE BLOCKS TRUMP'S MEDICAID CRACKDOWN ON THE SICK: “Great Hardship” Warning
dek: A Boston federal judge just stopped the administration from narrowing who counts as “medically frail” under Medicaid's new work rules, ruling the extra hurdle could strip coverage from seriously ill people.

title: WAR-DRIVEN FUEL BOOM HANDS EXXON AND CHEVRON A REFINING WINDFALL
dek: America's oil giants just beat profit expectations — and for the first time in at least six years, Exxon is making more money refining fuel than pumping oil.

title: CLOCKS FALL BACK SUNDAY: Trump's Push to Kill the Time Change Just Ran Out of Time
dek: Despite months of pressure from President Trump — including posting a senator's phone number — the Senate let the permanent daylight saving bill die, so America returns to standard time at 2 a.m. Sunday.

title: 60 COSTUMES, ONE MORNING: Kelly and Mark Go Full Halloween Marathon
dek: Live with Kelly and Mark turned its annual Halloween special into a rapid-fire costume sprint, with more than 60 looks packed into one episode.

title: SAMSUNG'S AI GLASSES ARE REPORTEDLY COMING IN DECEMBER: But Only in Two Countries First
dek: A new report tips Samsung's first AI smart glasses for a mid-December launch in South Korea and the US, with the rest of the world left waiting.

title: MYANMAR'S WAR, BACK AT THE TABLE: ASEAN Envoy Meets Junta Minister in Naypyitaw
dek: Southeast Asia's envoy on Myanmar met the country's foreign minister Thursday to discuss the civil war and humanitarian access, as Myanmar pushes to restore its standing in the bloc.

title: ROOKIE TAKES OVER: Cameron Boozer's First Triple-Double Keeps Grizzlies Perfect
dek: The rookie posted 18 points, 12 rebounds and 12 assists as Memphis crushed Portland 124-103 to stay unbeaten at 5-0.

title: DOJ WANTS TO BLOCK ALASKA CERTIFICATION IF THE GOP LOSES CLOSE: And Alaska Calls It Meritless
dek: The Justice Department filed an amended lawsuit October 30 seeking to block certification of Alaska's Senate race if Republican Dan Sullivan loses narrowly, alleging a spoiler candidate with the same name was recruited to confuse voters.

title: ADT SOLD FOR $15.3 BILLION IN BLOCKBUSTER TAKE-PRIVATE DEAL
dek: The 150-year-old home security giant is going private after Thrive Holdings agreed to buy it for $10 a share in cash — a 45.6% premium that sent the stock soaring 33%.

title: APPEALS COURT TO TRUMP'S ICE SURGE: “Why Do You Need This?” — Voter Crackdown Stays Blocked
dek: A federal appeals court refused to let Homeland Security restart its pre-election voter-fraud crackdown in nine states, questioning why the surge was rushed just days before the midterms.

title: APPLE'S HOMEPOD MINI 2 HITS SHELVES: But the Big Siri Upgrade Is Still Coming
dek: Apple's new smart speaker went on sale October 30 in India and more than 23 other markets, promising a smarter Siri that will only arrive in a future software update.

title: “REAL SNOOP WOULD NEVER DO THIS!”: Martha Stewart Scolds Craig Melvin Live on Today
dek: A Halloween cooking segment turned messy when chocolate ganache landed on Martha Stewart's white pants — and she did not let Craig Melvin off the hook.

title: WHILE THE WORLD BUILDS WALLS, CHINA AND SWITZERLAND SIGN A DEAL: Xi and Parmelin Hail Upgraded Trade Pact
dek: China and Switzerland hailed an upgraded trade agreement in Beijing on Friday, bucking the global shift toward protectionism and giving Switzerland unusually free access to Chinese markets.

title: BLOCKBUSTER OUT OF NOWHERE: Bears Land Jeffery Simmons for Two First-Rounders
dek: One late-night phone call from Chicago flipped the trade deadline — Tennessee dealt its star defensive tackle to the Bears in a stunner even Simmons didn't see coming.

title: JUDGE TORCHES DOJ BALLOT BID: And a California County Refuses to Play Along
dek: A federal judge rejected the Trump administration's bid to halt counting of California mail ballots it suspects came from noncitizens, and Riverside County said October 29 it could not set aside 1,355 disputed ballots as demanded.

title: ECONOMY BEATS EXPECTATIONS WITH 3.4% GROWTH: But Inflation Is Still Burning Hot
dek: The last big economic snapshot before the midterms is a mixed bag: growth accelerated to its fastest pace in over a year, yet inflation climbed to 3.6% and stayed far above the Fed's target.

title: AMAZON KILLED THE FIRE TABLET: And Its Replacement Is a Full-Blown AI Tablet
dek: Amazon's October hardware rollout, recapped October 29, replaced its long-running Fire tablets with a premium Alexa tablet lineup that finally runs the Google Play Store properly.

title: THE INTERNET WON: Heat Give Dwyane Wade's Statue a New Face
dek: Two years after the original statue became a meme, Miami quietly replaced the head behind a plywood box — and Wade himself signed off on the fix.

title: 15-YEAR-OLD JAVITS FRIMPONG SHOT AND KILLED ON HIS WAY TO SCHOOL IN THE BRONX
dek: Javits Frimpong, who moved from Ghana about a year ago to live with his father, was shot Thursday morning in the Bronx. His father says he believes bullying at school played a role. Police have made no arrests and have not confirmed a motive.

title: MAKE IT SO, ONE LAST TIME: Sir Patrick Stewart Dies at 86
dek: From Shakespeare's stage to the bridge of the Enterprise as Captain Jean-Luc Picard — and as Professor X in X-Men — Stewart defined two of the biggest franchises ever. He died at his Los Angeles home after a brief journey with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia.

title: THE BIGGEST CRYPTO HEIST EVER: Binance Says $6.3 Billion Hit in Hack
dek: Binance says about $6.3 billion in assets was impacted in a security incident — dwarfing the $1.5 billion Bybit hack of 2025. About $3 billion has been frozen, withdrawals are suspended, and Binance says it will cover all losses.

title: THEE CIRCUS IS HERE: Megan Thee Stallion's Hottieween Takes Over Vegas Tonight
dek: Megan Thee Stallion's annual Hottieween party takes over Zouk Nightclub in Las Vegas tonight — a circus-themed blowout with Cirque du Soleil, special guest Uncle Waffles, and costumes mandatory.

title: SÍ, SE PUEDE: Labor Leader Dolores Huerta Dies at 96
dek: Dolores Huerta — the labor leader who co-founded the United Farm Workers with Cesar Chavez and gave the movement its famous slogan — has died at 96, her family announced.

title: CHARGED OVER A POLLING-PLACE STUNT: O'Keefe and Higby Face Felony Counts in Minnesota
dek: Minnesota prosecutors have charged conservative activist James O'Keefe and influencer Cam Higby with felony unlawful voting and identity theft over a hidden-camera polling-place stunt. Neither man actually voted, prosecutors say — but they say misrepresenting yourself while applying for a ballot is enough.

title: 13 KILLED AT A TRAIN STATION: Russian Drone Hits Passenger Train in Dnipro
dek: A Russian drone struck a passenger train at Dnipro's main railway station in central Ukraine on Thursday morning, killing 13 people and injuring 10 others, authorities said.

title: DEMI LOVATO SPEAKS OUT AFTER BRIEF HOSPITAL SCARE
dek: The singer says she had a brief hospital visit after a possible allergic reaction — possibly from passionfruit or sushi, though the exact trigger is not confirmed. She reassured fans she is doing fine after being discharged.

title: GRAND JURY SAYS NO: No Indictment for Cassidy Hutchinson Over Jan. 6 Testimony
dek: A federal grand jury declined to indict the former White House aide over her testimony to the congressional panel that investigated the Jan. 6, 2021 Capitol attack. Hutchinson has maintained her testimony was truthful.

title: BOLSONARO FLEES TO THE U.S.: Brazil Cancels His Passports After He Defies Court Order
dek: Days after Brazil’s presidential runoff, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro left the country for the United States after defying a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports. Brazil’s Federal Police have now cancelled them.

title: 50,800 DEATHS A YEAR: CDC Warns Drug-Resistant Germs Are a Growing Crisis
dek: The CDC’s new 2026 report estimates drug-resistant germs cause 9.7 million infections and about 50,800 deaths in the United States each year. Four germs are now rated “urgent” threats.

title: RAMA MEETS RAVANA: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash’s Hug Steals the Ramayana LA Premiere
dek: At the Los Angeles premiere of “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend,” Ranbir Kapoor, who plays Rama, and Yash, who plays Ravana, shared a warm hug on the red carpet. The film hits theatres November 5.

title: Are You Really a 'Bird' or You Just Love Hard?
dek: TikTok will call any girl who loves out loud a bird. But there's a difference between a bird and a girl who just loves hard — and most people calling names can't tell them apart.

title: Signs Ur Ho Going This Halloween
dek: Halloween is breakup season. Before the costumes come out, the signs show up first — distance, resources, attire, and the arguing that comes right before the breakup. Here's how you know the breakup is coming before the party even starts.

title: $1 MILLION FOR A TIP: Trump Offers Cash for Voter Fraud Reports
dek: One week before the midterms, the president says anyone whose voter fraud report leads to an arrest and conviction gets $1 million. He has not said who pays for it.

title: ISRAEL VOTES: Netanyahu's Survival on the Line in First Election Since Oct. 7
dek: Israelis head to the polls in their first election since the Oct. 7, 2023 Hamas attacks, with no bloc holding a clear path to the 61 seats needed to govern.

title: JAY-Z IS HEADLINING THE SUPER BOWL: Hov Picks Himself for Halftime
dek: After years of picking the halftime acts through Roc Nation, Jay-Z will headline the Super Bowl LXI halftime show on Feb. 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium.

title: FROM THE ER TO SEXIEST MAN ALIVE: Noah Wyle Takes People's 2026 Title
dek: The Pitt star and former ER doctor is People's Sexiest Man Alive for 2026. He thought the whole thing was a prank.

title: Nicki Minaj's a Dumb Ass
dek: She built a career off Black fans, then spent years cashing that love in for a seat at somebody else's table. The press secretary rumors just made it official.

title: RIP TO THE VOICE OF OUR CHILDHOOD: Eric Bauza, Voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, Dies at 46
dek: The Emmy-winning voice of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and so many Looney Tunes favorites has died at 46. Warner Bros. called him “a unique voice talent who brought joy and laughter to millions.”

title: JUJU IS BACK: Watkins Drops 18 in 23 Minutes in Return After 580 Days Out
dek: After 580 days out with a torn ACL, USC star JuJu Watkins returned Sunday and dropped 18 points in 23 minutes in an exhibition win over Cal.

title: HEIDIWEEN IS COMING — AND IT'S BLOODY: Heidi Klum Teases Her 2026 Halloween Costume
dek: The queen of Halloween teased her 2026 costume one week before her annual NYC party — a close-up of a grotesque prosthetic — and warned fans this year's look is “very bloody.”

title: LULA WINS BRAZIL: President Takes Historic Fourth Term With 51.76% in Runoff
dek: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva beat Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday's runoff, capping a comeback after trailing in the first round — while Bolsonaro refuses to concede and vows a legal fight.

title: Should Christians Celebrate Halloween? One Podcast Ignited a Holy War Over Candy, Tracts and Horror Movies
dek: Allie Beth Stuckey says believers should rethink Halloween and horror — and the backlash, from “stop being weird” to “horror is the most Christian genre,” has split Christian social media a week before Halloween.

title: France Erupts Again: Hundreds of Thousands March in Second Weekend of Protests as Police Flood Paris Streets
dek: Around 410,000 people marched nationwide — 110,000 in Paris alone — as 70,000 police deployed to prevent a repeat of last weekend's riots.

title: Fire Engulfs Hitler's 'Eagle's Nest' Mountain Retreat in Bavaria
dek: Around 200 firefighters battled flames at the historic Kehlsteinhaus on Friday. Police have detained a suspect.
